name: Green Flash
spirit: Bourbon (high-proof, e.g. Elijah Craig, Wild Turkey 101)
method: Stir all with ice 25-30 sec, strain over large cube. Flame the orange peel: hold skin-side out toward the drink, pass a lit match between peel and glass, then sharply squeeze the peel to spray the oils through the flame. Drop the peel in.
notes: Chartreuse replaces the sugar — no simple syrup needed. Start at ¼ oz, don't overdo it (110 proof). The flamed peel is the drink's namesake moment.
nameStory: Named for the green flash: an optical phenomenon sometimes seen at sea right at sunset over the ocean.

name: Spirit Room
ingredients: ½ oz Magic Syrup (brown sugar, toasted coconut, butterscotch extract, vanilla extract)
Graham cracker rim or toasted marshmallow garnish
method: Rim rocks glass with honey + crushed graham crackers. Stir bourbon, syrup, bitters with ice 30 sec. Strain over one large ice sphere into prepared glass.
notes: V2 improves on the original — single homemade Magic Syrup replaces separate coconut/butterscotch syrups.
nameStory: A ship's "spirit room" was the actual compartment where liquor stores were kept — kept as final name, no rename needed.

name: Marcy's Windfall
method: Stir liquids with ice until well chilled, pour over one large cube in rocks glass, garnish with nutmeg + banana chip.
notes: Use higher-proof bourbon (100+) or it can get too sweet.
nameStory: Named for the user's sister-in-law Marcy, who this drink converted into an Old Fashioned fan. "Windfall" = an unexpected favorable wind / unexpected good fortune.

name: Full Fathom Five
spirit: Split base — Knob Creek Smoked Maple bourbon + regular bourbon
ingredients: 1 oz Knob Creek Smoked Maple bourbon
method: Stir all with ice, strain over one large cube, express orange peel over the drink.
notes: Alt fat-wash version: 2 oz bourbon, ¼ oz maple syrup, 4 dashes Fee Brothers Browned Butter fat wash, lemon peel garnish — simpler build, worth taste-testing both.
nameStory: From Shakespeare's The Tempest — "something rich and strange."

name: Stipe's Even Keel
notes: Classic Old Fashioned with adjusted ratios for Stepe (Croatian, drink is a favorite of the ladies).
nameStory: "Even keel" = balanced and steady, fitting since it's the classic ratio rebalanced.

name: Roasted Duck Fat Boulevardier
ingredients: 5 dashes Fee Brothers Roasted Duck fat wash
method: Stir all with ice, strain, garnish with orange peel.
notes: Reintroduces the Boulevardier concept after the plain classic was removed — fat wash makes it different enough to warrant its own entry. Needs a nautical name.
source: Personal recipe (Fee Brothers Fat Wash Drops)

name: Bacon Vieux Carré
ingredients: ¾ oz cognac (or ~1 oz B&B liqueur as a simplified substitute)
4 dashes Fee Brothers Bacon fat wash
method: Stir all with ice, strain, garnish with lemon twist.
notes: Riff on the classic New Orleans Vieux Carré with a bacon fat wash added for smoky depth. Needs a nautical name.
source: Personal recipe (Fee Brothers Fat Wash Drops)

name: Cap'n Krunch
ingredients: 2 oz Cap'n Crunch-infused whiskey blend (3 cups Old Grand-Dad bonded bourbon + 1 cup Rittenhouse rye, infused 24 hrs with 2 cups Cap'n Crunch, then strained)
Piece of Cap'n Crunch cereal for garnish
method: Stir all (except absinthe) with ice, strain into absinthe-rinsed rocks glass, garnish.
notes: User wants to call this "Cap'n Crunch" on their own personal menu; kept as a neutral placeholder name in this tracker since it's a trademarked character. Riff on The Godfather, created by Patrick Jennings at Andra Hem, Philadelphia.

name: The Loggerhead
ingredients: ¾ oz Magic Syrup (same as Spirit Room)
Grated dark chocolate + pinch sea salt garnish
method: Dry shake all (no ice) 20 sec to emulsify egg/coconut cream. Add ice, shake again 15 sec. Double strain into chilled coupe. Top with chocolate + salt.
notes: Simplified from the original (crème de cacao + butterscotch schnapps) to reuse the Spirit Room's Magic Syrup. Flagged as very similar to Spirit Room — keeping both for now to compare after tasting.
nameStory: A "loggerhead" was the red-hot iron rod historically plunged into flip drinks to warm and froth them — genuine flip-cocktail history.

name: Kentucky Islander
method: Shake all with ice until chilled, strain into ice-filled chilled glass, garnish.
notes: Shaken/tiki-leaning rather than stirred — different profile than the rest of this category. Already has a nautical-flavored name.

name: Smoke & Brine Manhattan
ingredients: 1 oz sweet vermouth (Carpano Antica or Cocchi di Torino)
method: Stir rye, vermouth, bitters, and saline with ice 30 sec. Strain into rocks glass or coupe. Place under smoke dome (applewood/cherry wood) 15-30 sec, lift with flourish, garnish, serve.
notes: Variations to try: swap saline for a light fino sherry rinse (short shelf life — buy small format); or add a barspoon rinse of peated Islay Scotch for smoke baked into the liquid itself.
nameStory: States the drink's smoke dome + saline elements directly. Manhattan itself is reached by water.

name: Squall Line
ingredients: ¾ oz Rittenhouse bottled-in-bond rye (or other 100-proof rye)
method: Shake all ingredients with cubed ice 5-8 sec. Strain over fresh ice in a double old-fashioned glass. Garnish with pineapple wedge.
notes: A rye-forward riff on the classic Jungle Bird.
nameStory: A fast-moving storm front — keeps the punchy "Thunder" energy of the original name (formerly Thunder Bird), fully nautical.

name: The Dead Reckoning
ingredients: 1 oz House Amaro Mix (equal parts Amaro Montenegro + Averna or Ramazzotti)
method: Combine all in a shaker with ice, shake vigorously 12-15 sec, fine-strain into chilled coupe, garnish.
notes: Riff on the classic Paper Plane — swaps a house amaro blend for Amaro Nonino, adds Fernet-Branca for extra bitterness.
nameStory: Dead reckoning: navigating by estimated calculation rather than fixed landmarks — fitting since this riff estimates the classic's amaro component with a substitute blend.

name: The Undertow
method: Add all ingredients to a cocktail shaker with ice, shake, strain into ice-filled highball glass. Garnish with lemon wheel.
notes: Single-serving conversion from a batch recipe (serves 4: 6 oz bourbon, 4 oz grapefruit juice, 2 oz lemon juice, 3 oz honey-pineapple syrup).
nameStory: Undertow: a hidden, powerful current beneath the surface — echoes the "unexpected strength" idiom of the original name, Dark Horse.

name: The Siren's Call
spirit: Split base — rye whiskey + dark rum (50% ABV)
ingredients: ¾ oz sweet vermouth (Punt e Mes)
method: Stir all ingredients with fresh ice for a full 30 seconds. Strain over one large ice cube into a Double Old Fashioned glass.
notes: Split-base riff on the Boulevardier — dark rum replaces half the whiskey, Aperol replaces Campari for brighter, less medicinal bitterness. Garnish: "Siren's Sail" — wide orange peel cut into a sail shape, pierced with a black bamboo pick.
nameStory: Mythological sea sirens, luring with sweetness then holding captive with bitterness.

name: Ladybird's Landfall
ingredients: 3-4 fresh raspberries (muddled) or ½ oz raspberry liqueur
method: Muddle raspberries in a shaker if using fresh. Add gin, hibiscus syrup, and lemon juice with ice. Shake well, double strain into a chilled coupe or over ice in a rocks glass. Top with soda if using. Garnish with blackberries on a pick.
notes: Combines hibiscus (deep red, tart) with raspberry/blackberry (fruit character, dark "spot" garnish) — visually a deep magenta/ruby red.
nameStory: Named for the user's daughter McKenna ("BooBoo"), ladybug theme. Ladybirds are documented to swarm across open water during migration (the 1976 UK ladybird invasion) — "landfall" nods to that journey's end.

name: Bow Wave / Sea Spray
ingredients: ¾ oz aquafaba (or ½ oz egg whites — pasteurized liquid preferred; or Fee Foam methylcellulose foamer, 1-3 dashes/~0.3mL per drink)
Edible flower or citrus peel garnish
method: Combine all ingredients except soda water in a shaker. Dry shake (no ice) to emulsify. Add ice, shake again to chill. Strain into Collins glass over fresh ice. Top with soda. Garnish.
notes: Two name options to compare after tasting — Bow Wave (as-is, no salt) or Sea Spray (same recipe + a pinch of salt added).
nameStory: Bow Wave = the curling, foamy wave a ship pushes ahead of its bow, matching the foam cap. Sea Spray = fine mist off breaking waves.

name: Dragonfly-themed cocktail
notes: Dragonfly theme to develop.

name: Land Ho!
method: Shake tequila, Campari, passion fruit syrup, and lemon juice with ice until well chilled. Strain into a highball glass filled with ice cubes. Top with grapefruit soda, garnish.
notes: A Paloma riff created by Ryan Ota (Paper Plane, San Jose). Don't over-shake — leave room to top with soda.
nameStory: The classic sailor's cry upon first sighting land; ties to the historical tradition of doves/pigeons signaling land was near, echoing "Colomba"/dove and its Paloma namesake.

name: Midwatch Sour
ingredients: 1 tbsp Campari (or other red bitter aperitivo)
method: Add all ingredients to a shaker with ice, shake. Strain into a rocks glass over fresh ice, garnish with cocktail cherry (or two).
notes: Created by Pete St. Pete, Beverage Director at Capri Club.
nameStory: Midwatch: the real naval term for the overnight watch, midnight to 4am — fits a late-night pour.

name: The Sozzled Sandpiper
method: Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass, add ice, stir ~20 sec. Strain into Nick & Nora glass. Atomize a lemon peel above the drink so oils coat the rim, then discard peel. Garnish.
notes: Created by Cello Ritondo, lead bartender at Next Door by Wegmans (NYC). Inspired by the traditional Vesper + Japanese cuisine. Pairs well with sashimi/maki.
nameStory: Coastal bird theme (sandpiper) + "sozzled" (drunk slang), matching the boozy Vesper-style profile.

name: Ahoy Molly
method: Add vermouth, absinthe, and orgeat to a highball glass, stir to combine. Fill glass with ice, top with soda water. Garnish with mint sprig.
notes: Created by Sother Teague, beverage director at Amor y Amargo (NYC). Dolin Blanc has 32 botanicals including hibiscus, basil, and cinnamon.
nameStory: Nautical greeting, named for the user's niece Molly.

name: Mad Captain
ingredients: Lime wedge or coconut flakes garnish
method: Shake rum, lime juice, coconut cream (+ simple syrup if using) vigorously with ice. Double strain into chilled glass. Top with coconut water to taste.
notes: Chill glass first (coupe or rocks both work).
nameStory: Nautical.

name: Navy Grog
method: Chill a double old-fashioned glass or tiki mug. Combine rums, lime juice, grapefruit juice, and honey mix (+ bitters if using) in a shaker with ice; shake ~20 sec. Fill glass with fresh crushed ice, pour drink in, top with club soda, stir gently.
notes: Family taste-tested: Cath 10/10, Peter 9/10, Laurie 8.7/10. Based on Don the Beachcomber's classic Navy Grog. Garnish: lime wheel/twist, mint sprig, or spent lime shell.
nameStory: Classic tiki drink, already nautical.

name: Powder Monkey (Big Poppa's Return)
ingredients: Pineapple wedge or banana chip garnish
method: Shake all hard with ice, strain into tiki mug or rocks glass over crushed ice, garnish.
notes: Modeled on the version at CANE TiKi Room, Paso Robles ($16 on their menu). Exact proportions aren't published — this is a best-estimate clone to taste-test and adjust.
nameStory: "Powder monkey" = historic term for the young sailors who carried gunpowder to a ship's cannons. Nods to Peter's nickname "Big Poppa."
